content: 1. The endpoint of this method is not the complete dissolution of the tablet but rather the measurement of residue after a fixed disintegration time. This is particularly relevant for bubbling and opaque suspensions. 2. To prepare a dispersion of 100 to 250 mL at the maximum recommended use rate, weigh the appropriate amount of tablet(s). If necessary, break or cut the tablet, but do not grind it. Add the required tablet(s) or fragments to 100–250 mL of CIPAC standard water D at 25 ± 5°C and stir gently at 200 rpm for the time specified by the manufacturer. If no stirring time is specified, stir for 10 minutes. Proceed with the wet sieving method as described. 3. Before conducting the suspensibility test, ensure the tablet(s) or fragments are completely disintegrated in a 250 mL beaker containing 50 mL of the required water. Weigh the appropriate amount of tablet(s) or fragments to prepare 250 mL of suspension in water. Break or cut the tablet if necessary, but do not grind it. Add the weighed sample to a 250 mL beaker containing 50 mL of CIPAC standard water D at 25 ± 5°C and stir gently with a spatula until fully dispersed. Carefully transfer the suspension into a 250 mL measuring cylinder, rinsing the beaker with CIPAC standard water D to achieve a final volume of 250 mL. Stopper the cylinder and proceed with sedimentation determination as described. 4. The formulation should be tested at the maximum use rate recommended by the supplier. If the dimensions of the fragments prevent exact weighing of the required amount, an excess of up to 120% of the recommended use rate is permissible. 5. Chemical assay is the only fully reliable method to measure the mass of active ingredient remaining in suspension. However, a simpler gravimetric method may be used routinely, provided it has been shown to yield results equivalent to those of chemical assay. In case of dispute, chemical assay shall be the reference method. 6. Grind the tablet or its fragments into a fine powder using a mortar and pestle. Weigh the appropriate amount of powder required for 200 mL of water. Add 150–180 mL of CIPAC standard water D to a 250 mL beaker. Introduce the powder into the beaker and stir gently with a spatula until the sample is fully dissolved. Carefully transfer the solution into a 250 mL measuring cylinder, rinsing the beaker with CIPAC standard water D to achieve a final volume of 200 mL. Stopper the cylinder and follow the specified method. 7. This requirement describes the physical state of the tablet, such as whether it is broken, dusty with fragments, or soft and sticky. This is determined through visual observation only. Unless otherwise indicated, at least one package containing multiple tablets should be inspected for color, texture, fragments, and dust. 8. An attrition test is required only for bulk-packaged tablets with a diameter of less than 1 cm that may exhibit surface wear during transport and handling. This test measures the attrition resistance of water-dispersible granules but is also applicable to DT, WT, and ST tablets with a diameter of less than 1 cm. 9. Unless otherwise specified, alternative storage conditions include: 6 weeks at 45 ± 2°C, 8 weeks at 40 ± 2°C, 12 weeks at 35 ± 2°C, or 18 weeks at 30 ± 2°C. Whole tablets must be stored under these conditions. After storage, tablets may be broken for testing as specified, but no pressure should be applied to the sample during aging. 10. Both as-made and aged samples should be analyzed concurrently to minimize analytical error.
